source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Text-davinci-003 (GPT-3) matched or beat UCLA undergraduates on new text-only Raven-style Digit Matrices, and its error pattern by rule type resembled humans.
numbers: Digit Matrices, humans N=40: generative OR=1.88 (p=0.005, CI 1.21-2.91); multiple choice OR=6.27 (p=2.3e-8). Item-level correlation GPT-3 vs human r(30)=0.39, p=0.027. Best human got every item right.
limits: Digits are pseudo-symbolic; no visual parsing. Later challenged by counterfactual alphabets (c03, c04, c05).
agent_relevance: Source-to-target rule transfer on novel formal items is within reach of a plain model; do not rely on this for unfamiliar symbol systems.

source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: On story analogies (Gentner materials) GPT-3 chose the causally matching story above chance in near analogies but not significantly in far (cross-domain) analogies. Humans did well in both.
numbers: Humans N=54: combined t(53)=21.3; near t(53)=21.5; far t(53)=16.7. GPT-3: near binomial p=0.0039; far p=0.065 (not significant). GPT-3 vs humans OR=0.37, p=0.0003; 15/54 humans were perfect. GPT-4 preliminary on 72 problems: much better, near-perfect near, more robust far.
limits: GPT-4 test was via ChatGPT web interface on the same 72 problems, not a full study. Two-choice, chance 50%.
agent_relevance: Far-domain carrying of a causal structure is the weak point for LLMs. Candidate inferences from a far source need an explicit structural check (O7).

source: Lewis & Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Re-ran Webb's letter-string analogies with permuted or symbol alphabets. Humans stayed high; GPT-3, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 dropped sharply, more as the alphabet moved further from the standard one.
numbers: 136 Prolific participants (2 rejected on attention checks), 14 problems each. Permutations n=0,2,5,10,20 and symbol alphabets; 70 samples per data point per model. On the standard alphabet GPT accuracy was generally below human accuracy (unlike Webb). Share of errors from an alternate valid rule: GPT-3.5 38.59%, GPT-4 22%, GPT-3 5.81%.
limits: Counterfactual comprehension checks showed models can still state successor/predecessor in the new order, so the drop is not only misunderstanding. Webb's reply (c04) shows code execution restores performance.
agent_relevance: Test any analogy-style transfer on a changed surface form. A pass on familiar forms is not proof of structure use (G3).

source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Reply to the critiques: on shuffled-alphabet letter strings, GPT-4 with self-written code execution reached roughly human accuracy; plain GPT-4 stayed low, matching the critics' results. Authors say the failure is counting letters, not analogy.
numbers: Humans N=99 (interval 1) and N=97 (interval 2). Plain GPT-4: 300 problems per interval. GPT-4 + code: 60 problems per interval, hand scored. 46% of GPT-4 errors used a valid alternative rule vs 39% for humans. Interval-size effect for GPT-4 + code p=0.066 (not significant). One cell: extend-sequence at interval 2, 9/10 wrong.
limits: Small code-execution sample. Code use is not a human-like route. Newer GPT-4 cutoff (Dec 2023) postdates the critics' problem set; authors checked with an older engine and a new alphabet with the same result.
agent_relevance: A tool (code) removed the bottleneck: the mapping step was fine, the index arithmetic was not. Offload exact checks to code, consistent with G5.

source: Hodel & West (2024) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Independent counter-test: GPT-3 fails simple variants of Webb's letter-string tasks (synthetic alphabet, larger interval) while humans stay high. Also argues the original items may be in training data.
numbers: Humans N=121 UW undergraduates; GPT-3 averaged over N=50 instances. Only 2 of 6 problem types (remove redundant letter, sort) were not hurt. Counterfactual comprehension check: GPT-3 kept at least 30% of original level on all but the predecessor task on the synthetic alphabet.
limits: Tested GPT-3 only (text-davinci-003), not GPT-4. Contamination is argued, not shown.
agent_relevance: Contamination and surface familiarity are live explanations for good analogy scores. Prefer fresh or mutated items for any agent-side check.

source: Musker, Duchnowski, Milliere & Pavlick (2025) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning
finding: New tasks map words (semantic content) to symbol strings, so the solver must re-represent concepts. Top models (Claude 3, GPT-4, Llama-405B) matched humans in several conditions but reacted differently to distractors.
numbers: Random Finals condition: humans fell by about 0.5 relative to Only-RHS; models also fell (Claude 3 -0.5, GPT-4 -0.8, Llama-405B -0.4). Models worse than humans there: Claude 3 coef -1.05, p=0.005; GPT-4 coef -2.79, p<0.001; Llama-405B coef -2.02, p<0.001. Prompt wording alone moved Only-RHS accuracy between about 20% and about 100%.
limits: Human sample recruited by email ($10); prompt sensitivity is very large, so model-vs-human gaps depend on wording. Authors say models give a how-possibly, not how-actually, account.
agent_relevance: Large prompt sensitivity means one prompt proves little. Check candidate inferences under several phrasings.

source: Musker et al. (2025) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning, appendix on chain of thought
finding: Chain-of-thought gave weak results for Claude 3 on these analogies; a worked example shows it did well 'intuitively' but worse when reasoning step by step. DeepSeek R1 solved the same example by testing alternative rules.
numbers: CoT tested across all experiments with several prompt variants; answer phrase present in 97% (structure) and 87% (content) of responses. R1 result is one example only.
limits: Anecdote for R1; no systematic reasoning-model test. Authors leave it for future work.
agent_relevance: Written reasoning can hurt analogy transfer. A reasoning model that tests competing mappings is a hint for operator design, not yet a measured effect.

source: Sourati, Ilievski, Sommerauer & Jiang (2024) ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives
finding: Benchmark of narrative analogies built from relational (system) versus surface mappings. LLMs recognise near analogies but fail far analogies zero-shot; GPT-4 was below chance on far analogies.
numbers: Binary choice, random 50%. Humans: near 97.9%, far 94.1%. Models averaged 75.0% on near and 39.6% on far. GPT-4 best, average 68.1%; SBERT worst, 42.3%. Humans scored 98.6/97.2/96.8/91.4 across the four partitions (mean 96.0).
limits: Narratives from a proverb dataset (ePiC); element extraction by GPT-3.5. Binary task, so some of the gap is distractor design.
agent_relevance: Models take the surface-similar story. Candidate inferences from a cross-domain source need a check that mapped relations, not shared entities, drive the match.

source: Sourati et al. (2024) ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives, guided prompting
finding: Solved demonstrations helped far analogies by close to 10 absolute points for GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 but hurt near analogies; far demonstrations helped slightly more. Chain-of-thought was tested with 2, 4, 6 demos.
numbers: Demo counts 0, 2, 4, 6. GPT-4 most stable (small gain on far, small drop on near). Increasing far-analogy demos gradually improved near detection too.
limits: Exact CoT numbers were in a figure not read; GPT-4 demo-type study not run for cost.
agent_relevance: Few-shot worked examples shift the model from surface to relational matching; the trade-off is a loss on easy near cases.

source: Sourati et al. (2024) ARN error analysis of GPT-4 rationales
finding: GPT-4's written reasons often named the right high-level message, yet the choice was wrong, or the choice followed keywords, or the message matched only the chosen story and was not mapped back to the query.
numbers: Three error types listed with examples in Table 6; no counts given in the text read.
limits: Qualitative, from free-text rationales.
agent_relevance: Explanation and decision can diverge. Do not accept a stated rationale as evidence the mapping was checked (G2).

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Analogical prompting: the model writes its own relevant problems with solutions, then solves the target. Beat 0-shot CoT and was competitive with hand-written few-shot CoT.
numbers: Average accuracy gain +4% across GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench with GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM2. Codeforces: GPT-3.5 reached 15% Acc@1 versus GPT-4 16%. BIG-Bench with GPT-3.5 (some table rows garbled in extraction): word sorting 66.8% 0-shot CoT, 67.6% 3-shot CoT, 68.4% self-generated; temporal sequences 40.4 / 44.8 / 58.0 for the first three rows; formal fallacies 55.6 for 3-shot and for self-generated.
limits: Gains small on some tasks. Costs more output tokens. Sensitive to prompt wording.
agent_relevance: This is source-to-target transfer done inside one prompt, with no check on the self-generated source. Cheap to use; needs an external check on both source and result.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners, scale effect
finding: Self-generated exemplars help only with strong models. With small models (text-curie-001, text-davinci-001) retrieved labelled exemplars were better; from text-davinci-002 up, self-generation caught up and passed.
numbers: GSM8K Table 4: strongest model column shows 5-shot fixed CoT 50%, retrieved CoT 54%, self-generated 57% to 61% (rows partly garbled in extraction; direction stated in text). Self-generated beat 0-shot and 0-shot CoT at all scales.
limits: Only the OpenAI family tested for scale; row labels in the extracted table are scrambled, trust the text direction.
agent_relevance: If the source is made up by the model, source quality limits the inference. Prefer retrieved, verified sources for weaker models.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners, failure analysis
finding: Manual audit of 100 GSM8K+MATH cases shows how self-made analogies fail: irrelevant or wrong exemplars, and a generalisation gap even when the exemplar was right.
numbers: 50 correct: 6 irrelevant exemplars, 9 relevant but wrong solution, 35 relevant and correct. 50 incorrect: 10 irrelevant, 12 relevant but wrong, 28 relevant and correct yet failed (12 generalisation gap, 8 over-reliance on a specific exemplar, 8 other such as calculation).
limits: Single-audit, n=100.
agent_relevance: Of failures, 28 of 50 had a good source and still failed: the transfer step itself needs a test, not only the retrieval of a source.

source: Yu, He & Ying (2024) Thought Propagation: an analogical approach to complex reasoning with LLMs
finding: Thought Propagation (TP): the model proposes analogous problems, solves them, then aggregates their solutions into a plan to fix or direct the answer to the input problem. A working LLM-agent loop that uses analogical transfer.
numbers: Abstract: +12% absolute optimal solutions in shortest-path, +13% human preference in creative writing, +15% task completion in LLM-agent planning. Creative writing coherence score with GPT-4 (Table 2 as read, columns may be shifted): about 6.2 to 8.0 across IO, CoT, ToT, TP, with TP highest; TP used 5 analogous problems plus the input (6 plans).
limits: The aggregator is the same model judging plans (self-evaluation) in most variants. Coherence scores are model-rated. 5-shot gave marginal or worse results than 1-shot for all methods.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to O7 in an agent loop. The aggregator is a model judge, which G5 warns about; the simulation variant (run plans in the environment) is the safer one.

source: Yu, He & Ying (2024) Thought Propagation, ALFWorld agent planning
finding: In ALFWorld, TP takes plans from similar tasks that succeeded and uses them for the current task. Variants using real environment trials to pick the plan (Simulation) scored highest.
numbers: Overall success: Reflexion 79.1; ReAct best of 6: 71; Act best of 6: 45; TP variants roughly 83.7 to 94.8, the best using Simulation. TP without a failure memory still gained a lot.
limits: Reflexion value reproduced by the authors; other baselines quoted from ReAct. Row labels in the extracted table are shifted, so the per-variant mapping is uncertain.
agent_relevance: Transfer from a solved neighbour plus environment feedback, not a model's opinion, gave the best result. Fits G2.

source: Yu, He & Ying (2024) Thought Propagation, shortest-path and layers
finding: Baselines (IO, CoT, ToT) often fail to find the shortest path; TP gives more optimal and valid paths and lower over-length. One layer of analogous problems already helps; two layers help a little more at higher token cost.
numbers: 1-layer TP has token cost similar to ToT. 2-layer TP best in Table 1 but gain over 1-layer is small. ToT fails to produce valid paths on PaLM-2 and underperforms IO on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
limits: Exact Table 1 values not captured here. Synthetic graph tasks.
agent_relevance: Depth of analogy search has diminishing returns; one hop is the cost-effective setting.

source: Hu, Storks, Lewis & Chai (2023) In-context analogical reasoning with pre-trained language models
finding: Recoding RAVEN perceptual features as text lets GPT-3 do zero-shot relational mapping close to human level. How the problem is encoded matters a lot.
numbers: Center sub-task: naming entity attributes with numbers gave 77.2% (GPT-3 175B); quasi-image and random naming reached at most 28.2% and 51.8%. Decomposition added 2.8 points for GPT-3 175B; OPT 125M rose 22.2% to 45.6%, OPT 1.3B 47.2% to 72.0%. Multi-component tasks: decomposing by component gave about +20 on average; GPT-3 reached 77.6/78.0/82.8/92.6% on L-R, U-D, O-IC, O-IG.
limits: Perception is given as clean symbols, not from pixels. Idealised domain.
agent_relevance: Re-representation (naming, decomposing) raises transfer accuracy, especially for smaller models; a cue for how O7 should present source and target.

source: Ushio, Espinosa-Anke, Schockaert & Camacho-Collados (2022) BERT is to NLP what AlexNet is to CV
finding: Zero-shot word analogies (SAT, UNIT, Google, BATS) with BERT, RoBERTa, GPT-2: LMs identify analogies to a degree but struggle with abstract relations, and results swing with hyperparameters. Even tuned LMs barely beat the older LRA model.
numbers: SAT has 374 items. Best models GPT-2 and RoBERTa; BERT did not beat word embeddings. Optimal scoring parameters depended on dataset.
limits: Pre-instruction-tuning era; word-pair analogies only, not structure mapping.
agent_relevance: Baseline for how far scale and tuning have moved since: relation-level analogy in 2021 models was brittle.

source: Wijesiriwardene et al. (2023) ANALOGICAL: a benchmark for long text analogy evaluation in LLMs
finding: Benchmark with six levels (word, word vs sentence, syntactic, negation, entailment, metaphor) and thirteen datasets; eight LLMs found analogy identification harder at each higher level.
numbers: Eight LLMs, three distance measures, thirteen datasets.
limits: Embedding-distance method, not generation; no per-level numbers read.
agent_relevance: Analogy difficulty rises with abstraction; supports testing inferences on abstract, not lexical, cases.

source: Jiayang et al. (2023) StoryAnalogy: story-level analogies from LLMs
finding: 24K story pairs with human labels for two similarities (entity and relation, from extended structure-mapping theory). Identification is very hard for embeddings and LLMs; ChatGPT scored about 30% on 4-way choice.
numbers: Multiple-choice: random 25%, humans 85.7%, ChatGPT about 30%; best LLM 37.7 points below humans. In generation, few-shot demos improved LLaMa by +28.4% and +27.5%; fine-tuned FlanT5-xxl matched zero-shot ChatGPT.
limits: 2023 models; ChatGPT and text-davinci-003 only.
agent_relevance: LLMs generate analogs more easily than they identify which are analogous; so a generated source needs an independent check.

source: Bhavya, Xiong & Zhai (2022) Analogy generation by prompting LLMs: a case study of InstructGPT
finding: InstructGPT can generate source concepts for a target and explanations of the similarity. Precise imperative prompts and low temperature worked best; question forms were worse.
numbers: Human evaluation of 1.4k generated analogies; the largest InstructGPT model reached human-level on analogous concept generation, with more room on explanation generation. Relative gains of 19.17% and 15.34% going from 0.3B to 1.3B; typo injection cost 3-7% relative.
limits: 2022 model family; human raters.
agent_relevance: Source generation is feasible at scale but sensitive to wording and temperature.

source: Yuan et al. (2024) AnalogyKB: unlocking analogical reasoning of LMs with a million-scale knowledge base
finding: Built about a million analogies from knowledge graphs; training on it improved small models on analogy tests and on analogy explanation.
numbers: 1,032,040 concept pairs, 943 relations; 97% of 200 sampled items judged correct.
limits: Mostly relation-level analogies; accuracy sample 200.
agent_relevance: Verified analogy banks can serve as retrievable sources; quality check by sampling is cheap.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs
finding: A case-based reasoning agent: stores past trajectories as cases and learns which to retrieve with a small policy, inside a planner-executor loop. Case memory helps most out of distribution.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3 (top-1), test 79.40%; DeepResearcher 66.6% F1, 80.4% PM; case memory adds 4.7 to 9.6 absolute points on out-of-distribution tasks.
limits: Planner GPT-4.1, executor o4-mini (o3 on GAIA), so results confound strong tools and models. No analogy-specific ablation of the mapping step.
agent_relevance: Retrieval of past cases plus a learned selection policy is an existing agent-loop form of analogy; the gain is mostly out of distribution, so test it on shifted items.

source: Brown et al. (2020) Language models are few-shot learners, as cited in Ushio et al. (2022)
finding: Cited by Ushio et al.: GPT-3 was evaluated on SAT analogies; Ushio found that GPT-3 did not clearly beat the older LRA model in the zero-shot setting.
numbers: Not read directly; see the full-SAT table in Ushio et al.
limits: Secondhand; check original before use.
agent_relevance: Early reference point for LLM word analogies.

source: Wu et al. (2023) Reasoning or reciting? Counterfactual tasks, as cited by Lewis & Mitchell and Hodel & West
finding: Source of the counterfactual comprehension check used to separate 'did not understand the changed task' from 'cannot reason in the changed task'.
numbers: Not read directly.
limits: Secondhand.
agent_relevance: Add a comprehension check whenever a transfer test is run on a changed surface.
